message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations you should know: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate: 75 mph (or 70 mph if posted).
• Urban interstate: 65 mph.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours (unless posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 2 must be in a rear‑facing car seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (except for emergency calls).
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and those under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Traffic Signal & Stop Sign Rules** | • Red light: stop before the line; proceed only when clear and safe.
• Yellow light: treat as a warning; do not run unless it would be unsafe to stop.
• Stop signs: come to a complete stop at the intersection or crosswalk. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on your right.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals; check mirrors and blind spots.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Stop for all vehicles when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• Vehicles may not pass the bus until the lights are off and the stop sign is retracted. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of driveways, on sidewalks, or in no‑stop zones. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18; helmets optional for adults but recommended.
• Commercial vehicles: additional licensing and insurance requirements. | ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety and road conditions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Keep a safe following distance** – at least one car length per 10 mph of speed. 4. **Check mirrors and blind spots** before changing lanes. 5. **Stay alert for pedestrians and bicyclists**, especially near crosswalks and in residential areas. If you need more detailed information—such as specific statutes, penalties for violations, or how to file a traffic ticket—just let me know!
